name: Public Enemy
hook: A political rap group whose production team built walls of dozens of samples, the sound the 1991 ruling made nearly impossible to afford.
blurb: Chuck D (Carlton Ridenhour), Flavor Flav, Terminator X and Professor Griff came together around Adelphi University on Long Island in the mid-1980s and signed to Def Jam. Their production team, the Bomb Squad (Hank Shocklee, Keith Shocklee and Eric Sadler), built beats out of dozens of samples layered on top of each other, loud and chaotic on purpose. 'Fight the Power' (1989), made for Spike Lee's film Do the Right Thing, mixes more than a dozen sources, including James Brown's 'Funky Drummer'. Their songs argued directly against racism and police violence. Their records are the high point of dense sample collage without permission. After the Grand Upright ruling in 1991, that density became too legally risky and too expensive, and the Bomb Squad's method is the clearest casualty of the ruling. In 1989 Professor Griff made antisemitic remarks in a Washington Times interview. They caused a public crisis for the group, and he left it for a time. That is part of the group's record and is stated here as fact.
